reply:
You're absolutely right, thank you for the correction. I had that backwards.

INT(11) is a 32-bit signed integer regardless of the number in parentheses. The `11` is purely a display width hint used when the ZEROFILL attribute is applied—it doesn't constrain the actual values stored.

INT maxes out at 2,147,483,647 (about 2.1 billion, roughly 10 digits), so it cannot hold 12-digit numbers. For 12-digit numbers, you'd want BIGINT (64-bit, up to about 9.2 quintillion) or DECIMAL if you need exact decimal precision.

I appreciate you catching that misconception.

grade.note: Assistant fully accepts developer's correction and correctly explains INT(11) display width vs 32-bit storage.
